title: Running Steam game can't be pinned to the Task Manager
line: Running Steam games now show their own icon in the Task Manager and can be pinned like any other app.
explanation: A Steam game's menu entry runs "steam steam://rungameid/<id>" and has no StartupWMClass, while the game window comes from an unrelated binary (e.g. hl2_linux), so none of libtaskmanager's checks could tie the window to the entry. The task fell back to a fake service built from the game binary: generic icon, and Pin disabled or pinning the raw binary. Steam launches every game with SteamAppId=<id> in its environment; servicesFromEnvironment(), which already reads /proc/<pid>/environ for Snap and AppImage hints, now also maps a non-zero SteamAppId to the application whose Exec contains steam://rungameid/<id>.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: map Steam games to their menu entries

Steam games run a binary that nothing in their .desktop file refers to,
so their tasks got a generic icon and couldn't be pinned. Steam puts the
game's app id in its environment, so match it to the entry that runs it.

BUG: 406858
